question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: Taking daily preventive antibiotics
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Spraying rooms with strong disinfectants
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves at all times

explanation: Simple soap and water (or alcohol rub) save lives! Good hand hygiene washes away hitchhiking germs before they ever reach a patient.

question: Which of these tasks is safe and appropriate to hand over (delegate) to assistive personnel?

options.A: Administering intravenous pain medication for acute trauma
options.B: Creating the initial nursing care plan for a new admission
options.C: Taking routine vital signs for a stable postoperative patient
options.D: Evaluating the healing progress of a surgical incision

explanation: Spot on! Stable patients and routine vitals are great for assistive staff, freeing you up to handle the more complex clinical duties.

question: When do expectant mothers usually notice that their vulval varicose veins hurt or ache the most?

options.A: Directly after a heavy meal
options.B: Immediately upon waking up in the morning
options.C: After standing or walking for a long time
options.D: While resting flat on their back

explanation: Gravity is the culprit here! Staying on your feet all day lets blood pool downward, so by evening, the pressure and ache feel much stronger. Rest and elevation are best friends here.

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in our special senses?

options.A: Pump blood through the sensory organs
options.B: Convert environmental stimuli into electrical signals
options.C: Store memories of past sensory experiences
options.D: Produce hormones to regulate body temperature

explanation: Think of sensory receptors as tiny translators! They take physical things from the world around us—like light or sound—and change them into electrical signals that our nervous system can easily read and understand.

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy village residents
options.B: To replace traditional healers with western medical doctors
options.C: To identify health needs and available resources in a population
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor environmental sanitation

explanation: A community diagnosis looks at both the health gaps and the existing assets of a population to guide future interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h1)

question: What regulatory body guides the professional practice and scope of nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Pharmacists Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria sets the legal boundaries and professional standards for all nursing practice in the country. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the medical term for a fever?

options.A: Hyperkalemia
options.B: Hypothermia
options.C: Pyrexia
options.D: Hypovolemia

explanation: Pyrexia is the official medical term used to describe an elevated body temperature or fever. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h2)

question: You check a preliminary scan report on a confused patient and discover an unexpected fracture. What is your best next step?

options.A: Notify the primary care provider or medical team immediately for follow-up orders
options.B: Place the patient in strict isolation to prevent further bone damage
options.C: Discharge the patient quickly before the family sees the report
options.D: Wait until the patient complains of severe pain before telling anyone

explanation: Quick communication is key! Letting the medical team know right away ensures the patient gets proper care and treatment for that surprise injury.

question: Under current Nigerian laws, when is a pregnancy termination generally allowed?

options.A: If the pregnancy results from consensual teenage dating
options.B: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases during the first trimester
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it in writing

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian laws are quite strict and typically permit abortion only when carrying the pregnancy to term puts the mother's life in danger.

question: Why is it important for the body to release hormones in pulses?

options.A: It ensures constant, unvarying blood pressure all day
options.B: It prevents receptor down-regulation and desensitization
options.C: It stops the nervous system from sending electrical signals
options.D: It triggers immediate humoral stimulation in the pancreas

explanation: If cells are flooded with hormones non-stop, they get 'numb' to them. Pulsing keeps the cell receptors fresh and listening!

question: Why do many patients prefer injections over oral medications?

options.A: Swallowing pills is physically impossible for most adults.
options.B: Injections are always cheaper than buying tablets from a pharmacy.
options.C: They believe injections work much faster and are stronger.
options.D: Government policies mandate injections for routine checkups.

explanation: A widespread cultural belief is that injected drugs enter the blood directly and provide a stronger, quicker cure than oral pills. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h2)

question: What crucial instruction should a nurse give to a pregnant woman diagnosed with a low-lying placenta (placenta praevia)?

options.A: Take iron supplements only when bleeding starts
options.B: Restrict fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.C: Avoid sexual intercourse in late pregnancy
options.D: Engage in heavy daily aerobic exercise

explanation: Avoiding activities that can disturb the lower uterine segment, such as sexual intercourse, helps prevent triggering sudden bleeding when the placenta is low. Simple and life-saving!

question: What is a main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To provide extra funding for international medical research
options.B: To allocate limited healthcare resources where they are needed most
options.C: To replace the need for individual patient physical examinations
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in private hospitals

explanation: Resources are always limited, so finding the highest priority problems ensures supplies and personnel go where they will do the most good. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical symptom category for patients with heart tumours?

options.A: Signs of heart failure like shortness of breath
options.B: Constitutional signs like fever and weight loss
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of taste
options.D: Embolisation symptoms such as a stroke

explanation: Loss of taste has nothing to do with heart tumours! On the flip side, heart failure signs, fevers, and stroke symptoms are classic warning signs. You've got this!

question: Which special layer of cells fuses together without distinct boundaries to burrow into the mother's tissue?

options.A: Syncytiotrophoblast
options.B: Decidua basalis
options.C: Inner cell mass
options.D: Cytotrophoblast

explanation: Don't let the big medical term scare you! The syncytiotrophoblast is a fused outer layer that acts like a clever pioneer, smoothly invading the uterine tissue.

question: In community health, why do leaders rely more on personal trust than strict job titles?

options.A: Formal authority only works inside large urban teaching hospitals
options.B: Community members do not respect official government titles
options.C: Volunteers and local leaders answer to community norms, not job descriptions
options.D: Health nurses are not allowed to give direct orders in villages

explanation: Since most people helping out in the community aren't clocking in as direct employees, building genuine trust and good relationships is key to getting things done. Great job thinking this through!

question: Which lab test is used to closely monitor standard unfractionated heparin therapy?

options.A: Prothrombin Time and INR
options.B: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: We use the aPTT test to check if our heparin dose is hitting the sweet spot—keeping the patient safe from clots without causing bleeding.

question: Why is it so helpful to teach elderly patients with chronic illnesses how to monitor themselves?

options.A: It helps catch worsening symptoms early before emergency care is needed.
options.B: It eliminates all normal age-related physical decline.
options.C: It completely removes the need for regular nursing home visits.
options.D: It allows the patient to change their prescription dosages alone.

explanation: You nailed it! When patients keep an eye on their own warning signs, little issues get caught early—long before they turn into scary hospital emergencies.

question: What is the main job of proteins in the human body?

options.A: Regulating the electrical rhythm of the heart muscle cells
options.B: Building and maintaining structural tissues, enzymes, and hormones
options.C: Providing the quickest and most immediate source of daily glucose
options.D: Storing excess chemical energy compactly inside adipose tissue

explanation: Proteins are the ultimate builders and workers. They make up our muscles, skin, and organs, and also act as enzymes and chemical messengers.

question: What happens during a chemical antagonism between two substances?

options.A: They react directly with each other to form an inactive compound
options.B: They compete fiercely for the same protein receptor on the cell surface
options.C: They alter the genetic DNA sequence of the target organ
options.D: They slow down the heart rate by acting on brainstem receptors

explanation: No receptors are involved here! They literally bump into each other in body fluids and neutralize one another, like acid meeting a base.

question: Which famous nursing theorist built her work around the patient's ability to perform self-care?

options.A: Callista Roy
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Madeleine Leininger

explanation: Correct! Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory focuses on stepping in to help patients when they cannot manage their own self-care.

question: What is the primary characteristic of a learning disability regarding a person's intelligence?

options.A: Intelligence is generally average or above average
options.B: Intelligence is below the measurable threshold
options.C: Intelligence is severely and globally impaired
options.D: Intelligence fluctuates drastically every day

explanation: People with learning disabilities have normal or high intelligence levels, but their brains process specific types of information differently. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses have to change how they normally work when responding to a field disaster?

options.A: Basic utilities and sterile spaces are usually missing
options.B: Patients refuse standard medications in the field
options.C: Disaster protocols completely forbid using medications
options.D: Physicians are rarely present during emergencies

explanation: Great thinking! Out in the field, you won't find normal hospital comforts like constant running water or steady electricity, so nurses have to adapt cleverly and safely.

question: Why is using standardized definitions for injuries and symptoms crucial during a disaster?

options.A: It stops patients from complaining about long waiting times
options.B: It allows doctors to avoid writing detailed patient progress notes
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients admitted to the hospital
options.D: It ensures that data collected from different clinics can be accurately combined

explanation: When everyone uses the same definitions, health authorities can trust the combined numbers from multiple clinics and hospitals. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement (QI) in nursing?

options.A: Cutting down nursing staff to reduce hospital costs
options.B: Punishing staff who make medication mistakes
options.C: Filing incident reports after safety errors happen
options.D: Proactively redesigning care to give patients better outcomes

explanation: Great job thinking ahead! Quality improvement is all about fixing systems before errors happen, rather than just reacting after things go wrong. You've got this!

question: A nurse sets up a free blood pressure check at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Primordial prevention

explanation: You nailed it! Secondary prevention is about catching health issues early through screening before they cause major trouble.

question: Why are elderly adults usually more at risk for catching infections?

options.A: Their skin becomes completely impermeable
options.B: Their immune defenses decline with age
options.C: They consume too many hospital medications
options.D: They have faster cellular regeneration

explanation: As people age, the immune system naturally slows down a bit, making it easier for germs to take hold. Great job thinking about your patients' vulnerability!

question: Why must patient assessment in palliative care be an ongoing, continuous process?

options.A: Because terminal illnesses and symptom experiences change rapidly over time
options.B: Because laboratory values fluctuate constantly during end-of-life care
options.C: Because hospital regulations require daily documentation updates
options.D: Because family members frequently change their minds about treatment

explanation: As serious illnesses progress, new symptoms pop up and emotional states shift. Constant checking and reassessing help us adjust care to keep the patient as comfortable as possible. Keep shining!

question: Why should the head of the bed stay elevated after a stroke patient eats?

options.A: To improve visual focus on surrounding room objects
options.B: To make it easier for the nurse to collect meal trays afterward
options.C: To reduce the risk of food or saliva entering the airway and causing aspiration
options.D: To increase blood pressure and prevent sudden fainting spells

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Keeping them upright stops food from slipping down the wrong pipe when swallowing muscles are weak.

question: How do a person's cultural and spiritual beliefs usually affect how they grieve?

options.A: They shape the expected rituals and public ways of mourning
options.B: They stop family members from feeling anticipatory grief
options.C: They shorten the time a person feels sad
options.D: They completely take away all anger and sadness

explanation: Culture and religion give people a comforting framework, ceremonies, and traditions to help guide them through loss.

question: How do informal support networks—like caring neighbors—protect vulnerable people such as the elderly?

options.A: By taking over their legal and financial responsibilities completely
options.B: By replacing the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: By moving all senior citizens into centralized government homes
options.D: By checking on them regularly and helping with daily tasks

explanation: Simple acts like checking in on grandma next door and helping with chores keep older folks safe, happy, and connected.

question: What is the main reason we incubate a clinical sample in the lab?

options.A: To remove all liquid content from the collected patient swab
options.B: To help any disease-causing organisms in the sample multiply
options.C: To preserve the sample indefinitely without any chemical changes
options.D: To kill all living bacteria present in the collected sample

explanation: Spotting an infection is easier when germs have room to grow! Incubation gives pathogens the warmth they need to multiply into visible colonies so we can test them.

question: What marks the transition period of adolescence?

options.A: Fixed behavioral patterns
options.B: The cessation of brain development
options.C: Complete emotional and financial independence
options.D: Rapid physical, emotional, and social changes

explanation: Adolescence is defined as a transitional phase marked by rapid changes across physical, emotional, and social domains. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is it important to check expiration dates immediately upon receiving new supplies?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of each individual item
options.B: To determine how many nursing staff members are needed on duty
options.C: To decide which shelf in the storage cupboard looks the cleanest
options.D: To prevent accepting short-dated stock that might expire before use

explanation: Catching expired or near-expiry goods upon delivery allows the facility to return them before accepting responsibility for wasted items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: A patient with a severe bone infection is losing weight rapidly despite resting in bed all day. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: Infections make the patient drink too much water instead of eating.
options.B: The patient's liver is storing too much fat for future use.
options.C: The body is in a breakdown state, using its own tissues for extra energy.
options.D: Bed rest causes the stomach to stop digesting food completely.

explanation: Severe illness triggers catabolism, where the body breaks down muscle and fat to meet the high energy demands of fighting the disease. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h2)

question: Why are nurse reports on side effects so crucial even after a drug has been approved for sale?

options.A: Drug manufacturers refuse to test their products before public release
options.B: Clinical trials cannot uncover every rare reaction before a drug is sold
options.C: Pharmacists do not notice any patient reactions inside the dispensary
options.D: Hospitals are legally required to fine patients who experience side effects

explanation: Exactly! Pre-market tests are limited, so frontline nurses are vital for catching rare side effects once real people start taking the medication.

question: What is the medical name for uterine fibroids?

options.A: Leiomyomas
options.B: Adenomyosis
options.C: Carcinomas
options.D: Endometriosis

explanation: You'll often hear fibroids called leiomyomas in clinical practice because they grow out of smooth muscle tissue. Great job keeping up with your terminology!

question: What are the tiny clumps of bacteria and blood clots that form on heart valves in endocarditis called?

options.A: Thromboemboli
options.B: Vegetations
options.C: Aneurysms
options.D: Atheromas

explanation: These little clumps are called vegetations. They form when germs and tiny blood clots (platelets and fibrin) stick together on a damaged heart valve.

question: In tubular secretion, where do substances move from and to?

options.A: From Bowman's capsule back into the glomerulus
options.B: From peritubular capillaries into the renal tubule
options.C: From the collecting duct into the renal pelvis
options.D: From the distal tubule into the loop of Henle

explanation: Spot on! Secretion is like a cleanup crew taking extra waste from the surrounding blood vessels and dumping it straight into the urine tube.

question: Why are local disaster teams so important when an emergency strikes?

options.A: They handle all federal immigration policies during a crisis
options.B: They are the first responders on the ground before national agencies arrive
options.C: They have unlimited financial resources to rebuild destroyed communities
options.D: They replace the need for hospital-based nursing care entirely

explanation: Spot on! Local teams are already right there where crises happen, making them the immediate first line of defense while distant federal help gets moving.

question: What term describes the condition where semen flows backward into the urinary bladder during climax?

options.A: Erectile failure
options.B: Azoospermia
options.C: Hypospadias
options.D: Retrograde ejaculation

explanation: Retrograde ejaculation happens when the bladder neck fails to close properly, forcing semen backward instead of forward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: A nurse notices that a physiotherapist and a doctor gave opposite advice on how a patient should walk. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Clarify the care plan by communicating with both professionals
options.B: Follow the physician's advice and ignore the physical therapist
options.C: Discontinue all mobility exercises until next week
options.D: Allow the patient to decide which professional to listen to

explanation: As a nurse, you are the communication bridge! Talk to both team members to clear up the confusion and keep the patient safe.

question: Why does cancellous bone remodel much faster than compact bone?

options.A: It has a higher surface area exposed to marrow and blood vessels.
options.B: It lacks any living cells inside its hard matrix.
options.C: It is made of softer cartilage instead of hard calcium.
options.D: It never experiences mechanical stress or wear.

explanation: Because cancellous bone is open and porous like a sponge, it has a massive surface area touching blood vessels and bone marrow. This allows cells to get in and out quickly, speeding up the remodeling process!

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand local Nigerian food habits?

options.A: It allows the nurse to restrict patient access to local markets
options.B: It serves as the best foundation for practical dietary recommendations
options.C: It helps the nurse completely replace traditional meals with foreign diets
options.D: It is only useful for hospital kitchen staff preparation

explanation: Great nursing care meets patients where they are! Working with familiar cultural foods ensures your nutrition advice is realistic, affordable, and actually gets used at home.

question: What is meant by a disease 'reservoir'?

options.A: Where the infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The Department of Health data storage unit
options.C: A device used to measure patient body temperature
options.D: The specific medication given to kill a virus

explanation: Correct! A reservoir is the natural hiding and breeding place—whether in humans, animals, or soil—where a germ thrives and reproduces.

question: Why is disease surveillance compared to an early warning radar?

options.A: It predicts natural disasters like floods that cause water contamination
options.B: It measures the exact wind speed during an airborne disease outbreak
options.C: It helps health workers spot unusual illness clusters before they spread
options.D: It uses satellite technology to track patient movements across borders

explanation: Just like a radar warns of approaching danger, surveillance detects disease spikes early so health teams can respond quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why does the pancreas release bicarbonate into the small intestine?

options.A: To stimulate the liver to produce more cholesterol
options.B: To lubricate the intestinal walls for easier transit
options.C: To break down protein chains into individual amino acids
options.D: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming from the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Bicarbonate is alkaline, meaning it cools down and neutralizes the harsh acid coming from the stomach so it doesn't harm your gut lining.

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during intrapartum care?

options.A: To test the mother's blood sugar levels
options.B: To register the baby's name after birth
options.C: To calculate the total cost of hospital delivery
options.D: To monitor the progress of labor and detect problems early

explanation: The partograph is a visual tool used by nurses and midwives to track labor progress and maternal-fetal well-being. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of an under-water seal drainage system?

options.A: To restore negative pressure in the pleural space
options.B: To measure the exact daily urine output of a patient
options.C: To pump sterile water directly into the lung tissue
options.D: To deliver high-flow oxygen straight into the chest cavity

explanation: The primary goal of chest tube drainage is to evacuate air or fluid, thereby re-establishing the normal negative pressure needed for lung expansion. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the main job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

options.A: To lower body temperature and decrease metabolic rate
options.B: To secrete progesterone and keep the uterine lining thick
options.C: To trigger the immediate onset of menstrual bleeding
options.D: To release a new batch of immature eggs into the tubes

explanation: The corpus luteum acts like a temporary caretaker, pumping out progesterone to keep the womb cozy and ready in case a fertilized egg arrives.

question: Why do nurses conduct a community diagnosis before launching a new health program?

options.A: It guarantees that funding from international donors will be approved
options.B: It helps identify the root causes and main health problems of the population
options.C: It allows nurses to avoid interacting directly with community leaders
options.D: It replaces the need for individual patient medical records completely

explanation: You got it! Checking the community first makes sure our interventions actually solve the real problems facing the people there.

question: What is the best and most reliable way to confirm a multiple pregnancy?

options.A: Maternal blood pressure
options.B: Ultrasound scan
options.C: Fundal height palpation
options.D: Stethoscope auscultation

explanation: Spot on! An ultrasound gives us a clear picture, letting us count the gestational sacs and heartbeats early on. Modern tech makes midwifery so exciting!

question: What is a major, non-negotiable requirement for a patient who has received a successful kidney transplant?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of physical activity to protect the new incision site
options.B: Undergoing hemodialysis twice a week to clean the transplanted organ
options.C: Following a strict low-protein diet for the rest of their natural life
options.D: Taking lifelong immunosuppressive medications to prevent organ rejection

explanation: The body's immune system naturally views a new organ as a stranger and tries to fight it. Transplant patients must take anti-rejection drugs every single day to protect their new kidney.

question: What does a modified radical mastectomy involve?

options.A: Removal of only the small tumor lump while preserving the rest of the breast
options.B: Surgical removal of the entire breast along with the axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Radiation therapy directed strictly at the skin without touching deep tissue
options.D: Daily administration of oral chemotherapy pills without any surgery

explanation: It means taking out the whole breast tissue plus the armpit lymph nodes to make sure the cancer doesn't linger locally.

question: What term describes the dangerous condition where a restricted patient breaks down their own muscle tissue?

options.A: Electrolyte poisoning
options.B: Hyperglycemic crisis
options.C: Protein-energy wasting
options.D: Fluid overload syndrome

explanation: When protein intake is too low or calories are insufficient, the body consumes its own muscles, leading to protein-energy wasting. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h5)

question: What is a safer alternative you can suggest to a new mother for easing perineal swelling instead of hot water?

options.A: Boiling steam directed continuously onto the surgical repair
options.B: Clean cold compresses or ice packs wrapped in a soft cloth
options.C: Total avoidance of any hygiene or washing for six weeks
options.D: Direct application of pure chemical bleach to numb the area

explanation: Ice packs are a nurse's best friend for fresh swelling! Cold numbs the pain and shrinks local blood vessels safely without burning or softening the tissues.

question: Why do nurses use splints and careful positioning for patients with polio?

options.A: To prevent permanent joint contractures and deformities
options.B: To speed up the regeneration of destroyed spinal motor nerves
options.C: To keep the patient completely immobile during ventilation
options.D: To stimulate blood circulation and stop muscle growth

explanation: You got it! When muscles are paralyzed, they pull unevenly. Proper positioning helps keep the joints safe from permanent stiffness.

question: What happens when stock levels drop below a safe minimum in an electronic inventory system?

options.A: An automatic reorder alert is generated
options.B: The hospital power generator shuts down automatically
options.C: All patient charts are locked until new stock arrives
options.D: The nursing supervisor's license is suspended

explanation: Electronic systems track thresholds and notify purchasing staff to reorder items before they run out completely. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which touch receptor is responsible for feeling deep pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Meissner corpuscles
options.C: Merkel discs
options.D: Ruffini endings

explanation: You nailed it! Pacinian corpuscles are large, deep receptors built specifically to catch rapid vibrations and heavy pressure.

question: A patient is admitted with sudden, severe confusion and mood swings. What must the nurse consider first based on biological etiology?

options.A: Whether an underlying physical illness or hormone imbalance is causing the symptoms
options.B: How long the patient has been using herbal sleeping mixtures
options.C: Which family member caused the patient to feel stressed recently
options.D: If the patient experienced a difficult childhood in the village

explanation: Medical issues like thyroid problems or infections can cause psychiatric symptoms, so biological causes must be investigated during assessment. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a very common emotional or social challenge for patients with chronic stress incontinence?

options.A: False belief that they are pregnant
options.B: Uncontrolled aggressive behavior toward caregivers
options.C: Severe memory loss and cognitive decline
options.D: Social isolation and anxiety about public leaks

explanation: The fear of leaking in public can make patients feel embarrassed, causing them to stay home and miss out on social life.

question: What is the primary focus of health maintenance?

options.A: Preserving wellness and preventing disease
options.B: Managing emergency room admissions
options.C: Providing long-term hospital rehabilitation
options.D: Treating advanced chronic diseases

explanation: Health maintenance aims to keep people well and stop diseases before they start rather than just reacting to sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following describes affective conflict?

options.A: An emotional clash driven by personality differences
options.B: A healthy debate over a new hospital protocol
options.C: A disagreement about medication dosages
options.D: A structural fight over ward budgets

explanation: Affective conflict involves feelings, ego, and interpersonal animosity rather than professional tasks. [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h6)

question: What key lifestyle advice should nurses give to help prevent osteoporosis in postmenopausal women?

options.A: Avoiding exposure to natural sunlight entirely
options.B: Following a strictly low-protein liquid diet
options.C: Restricting all forms of physical activity
options.D: Engaging in regular weight-bearing exercises

explanation: Activities like walking, jogging, or dancing put gentle pressure on bones, signaling them to stay strong and dense!

question: What skin color change is the biggest giveaway for severe oxygen deprivation?

options.A: Bluish skin discoloration
options.B: Flushed red skin
options.C: Spotty dark brown skin
options.D: Pale yellow skin

explanation: That bluish tint (cyanosis) shows up on the skin and lips when deoxygenated blood is pumping around. Always a vital sign to watch for!

question: Which of the following is NOT a barrier to effective communication?

options.A: Heavy use of medical jargon
options.B: Loud environmental noise
options.C: Severe physical pain and anxiety
options.D: Using simple and clear language

explanation: Using simple and clear language helps communication succeed, whereas noise, pain, anxiety, and jargon act as barriers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the five basic tastes?

options.A: Umami
options.B: Salty
options.C: Bitter
options.D: Spicy

explanation: Surprise! Spicy isn't actually a basic chemical taste. That fiery kick you feel is actually your pain and temperature receptors reacting to the pepper!

question: What happens in the body when a drug reaches 'steady-state' during regular dosing?

options.A: The drug stops working because the liver destroys all remaining molecules
options.B: The rate of drug intake equals the rate of drug elimination
options.C: The concentration in the blood continues to climb infinitely
options.D: Absorption drops to zero while excretion speeds up rapidly

explanation: Steady-state is a sweet spot! It means the amount of drug you take in matches the amount your body clears out, keeping your therapeutic blood levels nice and stable.

question: Why is having a written emergency plan important for families with vulnerable members?

options.A: It is required by law for every residential building
options.B: It lowers the monthly cost of utility bills
options.C: It stops equipment from breaking during storms
options.D: It prevents panic and guides quick action during a crisis

explanation: When an emergency happens, stress is high, so having clear steps written down helps everyone respond calmly and correctly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h8)

question: Why are AROM exercises great for keeping a patient's nervous system working well?

options.A: They require the brain to send nerve impulses that actively contract the muscles.
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any other physical therapy.
options.C: They stop the patient from ever feeling tired during the hospital stay.
