question: Why is the spinal epidural space considered a real space, while the cranial epidural space inside the head is just a potential space?

options.A: The spinal cord does not have any meningeal layers surrounding it like the brain does.
options.B: The cranial dura is tightly fused to the skull bones, whereas the spinal dura is not fused to the vertebrae.
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid fills the cranial epidural space constantly during daily life.
options.D: The spinal dura mater lacks any blood vessels or fatty padding beneath the bone.

explanation: You're learning fast! In your skull, the dura is glued tightly to the bone. But in your spine, there is an actual cushion of fat and veins around the dura, making it a true space.

question: You walk into a stuffy ward, fling the windows open to let in fresh air, and tidy up a messy bedside. Whose classic nursing theory are you putting into action?

options.A: Hildegard Peplau
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Virginia Henderson

explanation: Brilliant! Opening windows and clearing away dirt are the ultimate trademark moves of Nightingale's Environmental Theory.

question: What happens when illness or lack of water dries up the normal balance in the mouth?

options.A: Tooth enamel instantly repairs all of its own cavities
options.B: Bad bacteria multiply quickly and form dental plaque
options.C: The tongue changes its color to a bright lemon yellow
options.D: The salivary glands immediately shut down forever

explanation: When saliva drops due to sickness or dehydration, the protective shield weakens, letting nasty bacteria take over and build up as plaque.

question: What is the main focus of gerontology?

options.A: The manufacturing of mobility aids for the elderly
options.B: The surgical treatment of age-related diseases
options.C: The management of hospital finances for seniors
options.D: The study of the aging process and older adults

explanation: Gerontology is a broad scientific field that examines physical, mental, and social aspects of aging. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h1)

question: In the RICE first-aid treatment for sprains, what does the letter 'I' stand for?

options.A: Immobilization
options.B: Ice
options.C: Injection
options.D: Inflammation

explanation: Ice is applied early on to narrow blood vessels (vasoconstriction), which keeps swelling down and helps numb the pain. Great nursing intervention to know!

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders when promoting girl child education?

options.A: They work exclusively as classroom teachers in secondary boarding schools
options.B: They hold immense influence over local cultural norms and community acceptance
options.C: They are responsible for funding all primary health care clinics in rural areas
options.D: They write the national school curriculum and select all textbook titles

explanation: That's correct! Because local and religious leaders guide community beliefs, having their support makes it much easier to change attitudes and help girls stay in school.

question: How can a nurse best support an elderly patient with low literacy who takes multiple medications?

options.A: By stopping all medications until literacy classes are completed
options.B: By using pictorial charts and involving a reliable family caregiver
options.C: By writing complex medical terms down on a small paper slip
options.D: By telling the patient to memorize the pill colors and shapes

explanation: Visual aids like pictures and symbols overcome literacy barriers, while family involvement provides vital daily supervision and support. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the very first step when you want to develop a conceptual framework?

options.A: Drawing boxes and arrows on a whiteboard
options.B: Publishing the final research paper
options.C: Reviewing the existing literature on the topic
options.D: Collecting blood samples from patients

explanation: You always start by reading what other researchers have already discovered so you know what factors matter most for your topic.

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'nutritional deserts' in cities?

options.A: Dry geographic regions where no plants can ever grow
options.B: Neighborhoods that have an excess of community gardens
options.C: Industrial zones dedicated exclusively to meat processing
options.D: Areas with limited access to fresh, affordable, and healthy food

explanation: Correct! Nutritional deserts are urban spots where residents find it really hard to grab fresh, healthy food nearby.

question: Why must you always write down the body site (like oral or tympanic) along with the temperature number?

options.A: Different sites use completely different scales like Kelvin
options.B: Electronic health records will lock your chart without it
options.C: Hospital insurance demands the name of the device maker
options.D: Normal body temperature ranges change depending on where you measure it

explanation: Different parts of the body naturally run at slightly different baselines, so knowing the route is vital to read the results correctly.

question: What early symptom is typically caused by a tumor in the head of the pancreas blocking the bile duct?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Constipation
options.D: Vision loss

explanation: You're crushing it! When a tumor blocks the bile duct, bilirubin backs up into the bloodstream, turning the skin and eyes yellow (jaundice).

question: What is the primary instrument used during an otoscopic examination?

options.A: An ophthalmoscope
options.B: A sphygmomanometer
options.C: A stethoscope
options.D: An otoscope

explanation: An otoscope is specifically designed with a light and magnifying lens to view the ear canal and eardrum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is a common health intervention that voluntary agencies use to protect pregnant women and infants?

options.A: Providing heavy industrial machinery
options.B: Issuing international travel passports
options.C: Building commercial shopping complexes
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated mosquito nets

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is a big threat in Nigeria, so handing out treated nets to mothers and babies saves countless lives.

question: A nurse gets a positive rapid malaria test for a pregnant woman in a remote village. What should happen next?

options.A: Tell her to return home and wait for the fever to disappear on its own
options.B: Initiate the appropriate anti-malarial treatment protocol immediately
options.C: Ignore the result because rapid tests are never accurate
options.D: Send her patient file directly to the international health organization

explanation: Testing is only helpful if we act on the results! Once malaria is confirmed, starting treatment right away keeps both mother and baby safe.

question: What is the benefit of using standardized referral proformas in mental health care?

options.A: They ensure that all essential clinical and historical data is consistently recorded
options.B: They automatically guarantee financial sponsorship for the client
options.C: They eliminate the need for nurses to speak with clients or families
options.D: They prevent tertiary hospitals from ever discharging clients back home

explanation: Using standard referral forms makes sure no important medical or social history gets accidentally left out.

question: How does a stuffy, overheated lecture hall usually affect nursing students?

options.A: It induces lethargy and reduces cognitive processing speed
options.B: It improves their ability to memorize pharmacology lists
options.C: It sharpens their critical thinking and speeds up clinical math
options.D: It causes immediate hearing loss during lectures

explanation: Poor ventilation and high temperatures make everyone sleepy, which slows down how fast our brains process information. Keep yourself hydrated during long classes!

question: What is the main goal of doing a community risk assessment?

options.A: Punishing communities that fail to follow sanitation laws
options.B: Reducing the total number of practicing nurses in a state
options.C: Preventing illness and health outbreaks before they occur
options.D: Generating revenue for private commercial pharmacies

explanation: Prevention is our superpower in public health! Finding risks early helps us stop sickness before it even starts.

question: What is the main danger of a massive, uncontrolled bleed?

options.A: It drops blood volume and stops oxygen flow to organs
options.B: It blocks normal clotting completely
options.C: It triggers overproduction of red blood cells
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in blood pressure

explanation: When too much blood is lost, there isn't enough volume left to pump oxygen to vital organs, which can lead to shock. Great job thinking through patient safety!

question: What is the term for the normal, temporary hair shedding that happens after childbirth?

options.A: Androgenetic female baldness
options.B: Alopecia areata universalis
options.C: Hirsutism of the puerperium
options.D: Postpartum telogen effluvium

explanation: Fancy name, simple meaning! 'Telogen effluvium' just describes that normal phase where hair sheds after delivery before the cycle resets.

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for an infectious cervical irritation?

options.A: Eliminating the underlying pathogen with targeted medications
options.B: Numbing the pelvic nerve endings to eliminate pain sensations
options.C: Permanently removing the cervix to stop future infections
options.D: Increasing local hormone production through oral supplements

explanation: You got it! To fix an infection, we find out what germ is causing it and hit it with the right medication.

question: What does having 'psychological safety' mean for a nursing team?

options.A: Patients receive regular psychological counseling during hospital admission
options.B: Team members feel safe to speak up, question orders, and share concerns without fear
options.C: Wards are kept completely quiet at night to reduce stress
options.D: Doctors maintain absolute authority without input from nursing staff

explanation: Exactly! Psychological safety means even a junior nurse can point out a dangerous order without worrying about being insulted or victimized.

question: Where should physical family planning client files be stored when not in active use?

options.A: Inside an open bin near the clinic entrance
options.B: In the public waiting area bookshelf
options.C: In a lockable cabinet or secure records room
options.D: On top of the consultation desk for easy access

explanation: Physical files containing sensitive health data must be locked away to prevent unauthorized access by casual visitors or staff. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h5)

question: At what angle should a nurse insert the needle for a subcutaneous vaccine like measles?

options.A: At a 90-degree angle
options.B: At a 45-degree angle
options.C: At a 15-degree angle
options.D: Straight down at a 180-degree angle

explanation: Spot on! A 45-degree angle lets you place the vaccine nicely into the fatty layer just under the skin instead of going deep into the muscle.

question: A patient with diabetes looks shaky, dizzy, and is sweating before lunch. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Administer the scheduled dose of daily long-acting insulin
options.B: Send a blood sample to the laboratory for an HbA1c test
options.C: Encourage the patient to sleep until the symptoms pass
options.D: Check blood glucose levels and prepare a fast-acting carbohydrate

explanation: Shakiness and sweating are red flags for low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Always check the blood glucose first and have a fast sugar source ready! Patient safety comes first.

question: What is the number one, most vital treatment for a patient with cholera?

options.A: Immediate surgical intervention
options.B: High-dose vitamin supplements
options.C: Complete dietary restriction
options.D: Fluid and electrolyte replacement

explanation: Replacing lost water and salts (through drinking oral rehydration solution or IV drips) is what turns things around and saves lives!

question: What action must a nurse take before giving a direct IV medication through an existing line?

options.A: Increase the main infusion fluid flow to maximum speed
options.B: Disconnect the entire cannula and replace the dressing
options.C: Warm the medication bottle in a basin of hot water
options.D: Flush the line with normal saline to check patency

explanation: Flushing ensures the catheter is open, working properly, and clear of incompatible drugs before the new medication enters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why must everyone step back and not touch the patient while the AED is analyzing or shocking?

options.A: Movement can interfere with rhythm analysis or cause accidental shocks
options.B: Rescuers will catch the electrical current and stop breathing
options.C: The physical vibration of standing nearby stops the machine
options.D: The AED machine requires complete silence to function properly

explanation: Safety rule number one during an AED check: clear everybody! Movement tricks the machine's rhythm reader and can even shock the person touching the patient.

question: What is the main goal of community engagement in reproductive health?

options.A: Training foreign doctors to work in local clinics
options.B: Building more hospitals in rural communities
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment importation
options.D: Involving local people directly in addressing health issues

explanation: Community engagement focuses on working side by side with local populations so they can actively shape health interventions that affect them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: Where would you most likely give general health guidance to a group of people?

options.A: An isolated psychiatric ward
options.B: A crowded clinic waiting room
options.C: An intensive care unit bedside
options.D: A private, locked therapy room

explanation: Guidance is often broad and preventive. A busy clinic waiting room is a classic spot to share health tips with groups!

question: What is the biggest benefit of standardizing nursing workflows on the ward?

options.A: To increase the amount of daily paperwork required
options.B: To make clinical actions predictable and reduce cognitive load
options.C: To eliminate the need for physician orders in emergencies
options.D: To ensure all nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Standardization creates a comforting routine. When tasks are done the same way across the unit, you don't have to overthink every little step, freeing up your brain for patient care!

question: A clinic patient has a severe heart condition that your primary health center cannot manage. What should you do next?

options.A: Discharging the patient with instructions to rest at home
options.B: Telling the patient that no further medical help exists
options.C: Attempting advanced cardiac surgery directly at the primary clinic
options.D: Initiating a formal referral to a tertiary cardiac center

explanation: You nailed it! When a patient's needs are beyond your clinic's scope, safely referring them upward to a tertiary center is the best nursing action.

question: Why can a blocked intestine (bowel obstruction) eventually lead to a tear or perforation?

options.A: Trapped pressure cuts off the blood supply to the wall
options.B: The liver swells and crushes the intestines
options.C: Digestive enzymes dissolve the outside of the skin
options.D: Patients eat too much roughage while blocked

explanation: You nailed it! As contents pile up behind a blockage, the pressure squeezes the blood vessels in the intestinal wall until the tissue dies and tears. Physics and anatomy working together!

question: What is the best way to prevent accidental poisoning in community health?

options.A: Building specialized intensive care units in every village clinic
options.B: Educating families on proper chemical storage and prohibiting food-container reuse
options.C: Training traditional healers to perform emergency gastric lavage
options.D: Banning the sale of all cleaning agents and agricultural chemicals

explanation: Correct! Teaching families how to safely store items and never use old drink bottles for chemicals stops poisonings before they happen.

question: What is the main job of a Visiting Nurse Association (VNA) in a community?

options.A: Inspecting local restaurants for safety violations
options.B: Providing skilled nursing care and health education
options.C: Operating large regional acute care hospitals
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for home use

explanation: VNAs are set up specifically to send nurses out to homes, delivering expert nursing care and teaching families how to stay healthy.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for selecting an essential drug?

options.A: Bright packaging color and appealing flavor
options.B: High public health relevance
options.C: Proven clinical efficacy and safety
options.D: Acceptable cost-effectiveness

explanation: Aesthetic features like color and flavor do not determine whether a drug is medically essential for public health. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: How do micronutrients differ from macronutrients?

options.A: Micronutrients provide twice as many calories per gram as macronutrients
options.B: Micronutrients are only necessary during times of severe physical illness
options.C: Micronutrients are needed in much smaller amounts and do not directly provide energy
options.D: Micronutrients are manufactured inside the human liver rather than eaten

explanation: Vitamins and minerals (micronutrients) are like tiny sparks that help body processes run smoothly, even though they don't give direct fuel like carbs do.

question: What is the best bed position for a patient struggling to breathe who needs supplemental oxygen?

options.A: Prone position facing down on the bed
options.B: Semi-Fowler's or high-Fowler's position
options.C: Flat on the back with legs slightly raised
options.D: Trendelenburg position with tilted head

explanation: Sitting upright in Semi- or High-Fowler's position lets gravity help expand the lungs fully, making every breath much easier for your patient.

question: What does hormonal hypersecretion mean?

options.A: A complete stop in all hormone production
options.B: The excessive production and release of hormones
options.C: Normal hormone levels with sluggish target tissues
options.D: The destruction of endocrine glands by infection

explanation: Hypersecretion simply means an endocrine gland is making and releasing too much hormone into the blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which clinical situation typically requires the administration of emergency and critical care drugs?

options.A: Discharge planning for a patient with a healed fracture
options.B: Annual physical checkup in a healthy adult client
options.C: A sudden, life-threatening crisis like cardiac arrest
options.D: Routine outpatient follow-up for chronic mild headache

explanation: Emergency drugs are reserved for critical, unstable situations where rapid intervention is necessary to save a life. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h6)

question: How does chronic psychological stress typically affect food cravings?

options.A: It increases a natural desire for raw vegetables and water
options.B: It raises cortisol and triggers cravings for fatty, sugary foods
options.C: It forces the digestive system to absorb fewer total calories
options.D: It completely stops the body from digesting any proteins

explanation: You got it! High cortisol from stress tricks the brain into seeking out dense, comforting, high-calorie foods for quick energy.

question: A patient near a fast-flowing river has firm, painless lumps over their hip bones and very itchy skin. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Acute appendicitis
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Onchocerciasis
options.D: Malaria

explanation: You've got it! Those painless lumps (nodules) over bony areas combined with terrible itching near a river are classic signs of river blindness.

question: Experienced nurses are resigning in droves because they feel invisible and unsupported. What should management do first?

options.A: Stop holding staff meetings to prevent nurses from voicing complaints
options.B: Issue strict warning memos about the consequences of resigning early
options.C: Establish structured mentorship and recognition programs for clinical achievements
options.D: Reduce salaries across all departments to save money for recruitment ads

explanation: To stop nurses from leaving, you have to show them they matter! Recognizing their hard work and setting up supportive mentorship makes all the difference.

question: A patient with newly diagnosed severe kidney disease needs help managing their protein and potassium intake. Which setting is best?

options.A: Individual counselling
options.B: General television health ads
options.C: Group dietary classes
options.D: A public community workshop

explanation: New, complex diagnoses need one-on-one attention to review lab values and build a safe, highly specific meal plan. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h2)

question: What term describes the deep emotional exhaustion nurses feel from caring for suffering patients over time?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Compassion fatigue
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.D: Disenfranchised loss

explanation: Spot on! Compassion fatigue is real in nursing. It happens when you pour so much care into others without taking time to recharge your own batteries.

question: A nurse manager checks if staff are following the correct aseptic technique during wound dressing changes. Which type of standard is being evaluated?

options.A: Structure standards
options.B: Outcome standards
options.C: Process standards
options.D: Legislative standards

explanation: Process standards look at the actual steps and actions nurses perform while carrying out patient care duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: Which of these is a major home hazard that can cause older adults to fall?

options.A: Having too many windows in the bedroom
options.B: Loose carpets and inadequate lighting
options.C: Using electric fans during warm weather
options.D: Brightly painted walls in the hallway

explanation: Simple things like dim hallways or loose rugs are major tripping hazards. Home safety assessments are a key part of community nursing care for the elderly!

question: What is a major neurological risk for someone with poorly managed high blood pressure?

options.A: Increased production of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Spinal cord nerve degeneration
options.C: Cerebrovascular accident or stroke
options.D: Permanent loss of sensory nerve conduction

explanation: Constant high pressure can weaken brain blood vessels until they burst or block off, causing a stroke (cerebrovascular accident).

question: What does the catchy phrase U=U mean in modern HIV care?

options.A: Urinary excretion of unabsorbed medication
options.B: Unprotected union under treatment
options.C: Universal use of universal precautions
options.D: Undetectable equals untransmittable

explanation: Brilliant! U=U means when a person's viral load is undetectable through ART, they cannot sexually pass the virus to others.

question: What is the main purpose of the huff coughing technique?

options.A: To measure the total lung capacity of the patient
options.B: To force air deeply into closed alveoli sacs
options.C: To prevent the tongue from blocking the throat
options.D: To move mucus upward without collapsing the airways

explanation: Huff coughing keeps the vocal cords open while the patient exhales sharply, helping push mucus up from the lower airways safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h2)

question: In nursing, what does 'bundling care' mean when it comes to helping patients sleep?

options.A: Administering all daily medications at the exact same morning hour
options.B: Wrapping the patient tightly in heavy wool blankets
options.C: Grouping multiple care tasks together to reduce the number of times a patient is woken up
options.D: Sharing night shift duties evenly between nurses and assistants

explanation: Instead of waking your patient up every hour for a different task, you combine vital signs, meds, and dressings into one visit. That way, they get longer stretches of uninterrupted sleep!

question: What is the main difference between palliative care and hospice care?

options.A: Hospice care is delivered exclusively in large government hospitals
options.B: Palliative care is only for cancer patients, whereas hospice is for everyone
options.C: Hospice care requires stopping curative treatments, while palliative care does not
options.D: Palliative care focuses strictly on spiritual healing rather than physical pain

explanation: Think of palliative care as a companion to curative treatment at any stage, while hospice specifically steps in when curative treatments are stopped.

question: What is the main goal of the final routine postnatal visit at six weeks?

options.A: To conduct a comprehensive maternal check and discuss family planning
options.B: To remove the stitches from an uncomplicated vaginal delivery
options.C: To administer the baby's first polio immunization dose at birth
options.D: To measure the infant's final birth weight

explanation: Spot on! At six weeks, we do a full sweep of how mom is recovering physically and emotionally, and chat about family planning choices moving forward.

question: What is the biggest risk of waiting too long to report a sudden drop in a patient's neuro status?

options.A: It increases the financial cost of hospital room supplies
options.B: It causes the nursing documentation to look untidy
options.C: It can delay life-saving interventions for acute brain injury
options.D: It forces the patient to stay in the hospital an extra day

explanation: Brain emergencies move fast! Reporting changes immediately can be the difference between a full recovery and permanent damage.

question: Why do midwives frequently check if the uterus is firm after delivery?

options.A: To test the mother's abdominal muscle strength after labor
options.B: To ensure the uterine muscle is contracting well to prevent hemorrhage
options.C: To measure the exact amount of amniotic fluid left inside
options.D: To check if the baby is positioned correctly for feeding

explanation: Spot on! A firm, contracted uterus clamps down on blood vessels so the mum doesn't bleed too much.

question: Why should a food pantry be located away from the kitchen stove or oven?

options.A: To keep the kitchen floor clear of heavy storage bins
options.B: To protect the food from damaging heat and fluctuating temperatures
options.C: To ensure the pantry door opens without hitting the stove
options.D: To prevent the oven smoke from flavoring the dry goods

explanation: Constant heat from cooking appliances can spoil dry goods and make oils go rancid much faster. Keep them cool!

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the difference between the incubation period and the latent period?

options.A: Symptoms always start at the exact same hour infectiousness begins
options.B: Latent periods only apply to non-infectious chronic illnesses
options.C: Incubation periods tell nurses when to discharge patients
options.D: A person may be able to spread the disease before showing any symptoms

explanation: Exactly! Sometimes the latent period is shorter than the incubation period, meaning someone can spread an infection while still feeling completely well.

question: Why is it important for nurses to study both morbidity and mortality statistics together?

options.A: To prove that nobody gets sick in rural areas
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient examinations
options.C: To see which illnesses cause suffering versus which ones cause death
options.D: To calculate the exact salary of medical doctors

explanation: Looking at both illness rates and death rates provides a complete picture of the total health burden affecting a population. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: At 20 weeks pregnant, a patient's serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL. What does this result suggest?

options.A: Severe maternal dehydration
options.B: Normal kidney function for pregnancy
options.C: Potential underlying renal impairment
options.D: A normal non-pregnant baseline

explanation: Because kidney filtration speeds up during pregnancy, normal creatinine levels actually drop below 1.0 mg/dL. A value of 1.0 mg/dL means the kidneys might not be clearing waste as well as they should right now.

question: What should the nurse do before bringing a meal tray to a patient who needs feeding help?

options.A: Restrict all fluids until the meal is finished
options.B: Clear the bedside table and clean your hands
options.C: Give a sleeping pill to calm them down
options.D: Insist that family members feed every meal

explanation: Spot on! Basic hygiene and a clean, clutter-free space make mealtime safe and much more inviting.

question: What is the primary goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic adult illnesses
options.B: To provide free accommodation for teachers
options.C: To replace local hospitals within rural communities
options.D: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff

explanation: The core purpose of the programme is safeguarding the physical, mental, and social health of the school population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is 'moral distress' in nursing?

options.A: The physical exhaustion caused by working long shifts in the ward
options.B: Disagreements between nurses regarding shift schedules
options.C: The emotional pain of knowing the right action but being unable to perform it
options.D: The sadness a nurse feels when a patient passes away peacefully

explanation: Moral distress happens when you know clearly what is best for your patient in your heart and training, but hospital rules, doctors, or lack of resources stop you from doing it.

question: What does a 'cold' nodule on a radioactive thyroid scan usually mean?

options.A: A hyperactive area that is producing excessive thyroid hormones
options.B: An allergic reaction to the contrast dye used during imaging
options.C: A normal section of tissue unaffected by the radioactive tracer
options.D: An area of low metabolic activity with a higher cancer risk

explanation: A 'cold' spot means the tissue didn't soak up the tracer well. That sluggish activity can sometimes point toward a higher risk of malignancy, requiring a closer look.

question: What major change happens to the liver tissue during cirrhosis?

options.A: Overgrowth of active healthy hepatocytes
options.B: Replacement of normal tissue with permanent scar tissue
options.C: Enlargement of bile storage ducts
options.D: Complete disappearance of the hepatic artery

explanation: Think of cirrhosis as chronic injury that causes the soft working tissue of the liver to turn into hard scar tissue (fibrosis).

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental rules, including safe hospital waste disposal?

options.A: National football federation
options.B: Agricultural research council
options.C: NESREA
options.D: Federal road safety commission

explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) is the body that makes sure hospitals and businesses manage their waste safely in Nigeria.

question: Why should you check back in after a conflict has supposedly been settled?

options.A: To punish anyone who failed to follow the new rules
options.B: To write a formal disciplinary report for the human resources file
options.C: To verify that the agreed solution is actually working in practice
options.D: To ensure the conflict is brought up again at the next meeting

explanation: Agreements look great on paper, but a quick follow-up ensures people are actually following through during busy shifts.

question: How do standard expectorants typically trigger increased fluid secretion in the lungs?

options.A: By stopping the production of white blood cells in the chest
options.B: By mildly irritating the gastric mucosa to trigger reflex pathways
options.C: By directly binding to receptors on the surface of lung alveoli
options.D: By freezing the mucus so it cracks and breaks apart easily

explanation: It's a clever body trick! Traditional expectorants cause a tiny bit of irritation in the stomach, which sends a reflex signal to the respiratory glands to release more watery fluid.

question: What nutritional guidance should a home health nurse give to a newly postpartum breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Stop drinking water with meals to prevent overhydration.
options.B: Increase daily calorie and fluid intake to support milk production.
options.C: Avoid all dairy products to improve the baby's digestion.
options.D: Immediately start a strict low-calorie diet to lose pregnancy weight.

explanation: Breastfeeding burns extra calories and requires higher fluid intake to maintain a healthy milk supply and keep the mother energized. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which part of a used mask is safe to touch when taking it off?

options.A: The metal nose bridge exterior
options.B: The bottom edge near the chin
options.C: The straps, ties, or ear loops
options.D: The front center filtration panel

explanation: Always grab the straps! The front of the mask holds onto trapped germs and should never be touched directly.

question: What is the primary goal of performing last offices?

options.A: To treat the body with dignity and respect
options.B: To sanitize the hospital ward completely
options.C: To train junior student nurses on anatomy
options.D: To prepare the body immediately for autopsy

explanation: Last offices are carried out primarily to ensure the deceased person is handled with respect, care, and dignity. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: A patient with damage to the basal ganglia is most likely to struggle with which aspect of movement?

options.A: Reflexively pulling a hand away from a hot stove
options.B: Feeling the texture of an object in their hand
options.C: Smoothing out and coordinating voluntary actions
options.D: Breathing automatically during sleep

explanation: Because the basal ganglia regulate the fine-tuning and coordination of voluntary movement, damage leads to problems like stiffness, slowness, or involuntary tremors. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h3)

question: While helping a patient walk, you notice their urine bag is hanging higher than their bladder. Why is this a problem?

options.A: Urine can flow backward into the bladder and cause an infection
options.B: The urine output will instantly turn bright red with blood
options.C: The plastic collection tubing will melt from body heat
options.D: The catheter balloon will automatically pop from the extra pressure

explanation: Gravity works both ways! If the bag is higher than the bladder, contaminated urine can flow right back inside and give the patient a nasty urinary tract infection.

question: What is the main focus of end-of-life care when a patient is being cared for at home?

options.A: Complete reversal of chronic terminal diseases
options.B: Strict physical rehabilitation exercises
options.C: Aggressive curative surgeries and treatments
options.D: Comfort, pain control, and symptom management

explanation: Great job! At the end of life, the priority shifts completely from chasing cures to making sure the patient is free of pain and as comfortable as possible.

question: A researcher compares lung function in patients who developed chronic bronchitis against those who did not, looking back at their past smoking habits. Which design is this?

options.A: Cross-sectional design
options.B: Ex post facto design
options.C: True experimental design
options.D: Descriptive survey design

explanation: Well done! Because the health condition already happened and the researcher is digging into past history, it is an ex post facto (after the fact) study.

question: What is a key focus of antenatal care specifically for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Nutritional support and close monitoring for anemia and hypertension
options.B: Encouraging unassisted home deliveries to lower hospital costs
options.C: Avoiding all physical exercise throughout the entire pregnancy
options.D: Strict community isolation to avoid social stigma and gossip

explanation: Correct! Since teens are still growing themselves, they need extra nutrition and close checks for blood pressure and iron levels. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h5)

question: What word do we use for the strength of the attraction between a drug and its target receptor?

options.A: Efficacy
options.B: Tolerance
options.C: Affinity
options.D: Potency

explanation: Affinity is just like how strongly a magnet is drawn to metal. It describes how tightly a drug wants to bind to its specific cellular receptor!

question: Which home monitoring task is most critical for a patient undergoing chemotherapy who is at risk for infection?

options.A: Checking body temperature daily
options.B: Measuring blood pressure every four hours
options.C: Testing urine sugar levels twice a day
options.D: Weighing oneself every morning before eating

explanation: Because fever is often the only sign of neutropenic infection, daily temperature tracking is vital for catching early sepsis risks. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is another popular name for schistosomiasis?

options.A: River blindness
options.B: Chagas disease
options.C: Snail fever
options.D: Sleeping sickness

explanation: You'll often hear schistosomiasis called 'snail fever' because freshwater snails act as the crucial temporary home where the parasites grow during their life cycle. Great job remembering this!

question: Why is scolding or shouting at a returning defaulter a risky practice for a nurse?

options.A: It discourages the client from ever seeking care at that facility again
options.B: It violates international trade agreements
options.C: It instantly invalidates the chemical composition of oral pills
options.D: It causes immediate physical injury to the client's skin

explanation: Nobody wants to walk back into a place where they'll be judged. A welcoming attitude keeps our clinic doors open to those who need us most.

question: What is the primary tool midwives use to track the progress of labour on a chart?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Growth curve
options.C: Bishoff scale
options.D: Apgar chart

explanation: The partograph gives us a neat visual story of how labour is going. It's our best friend for spotting slow progress or fetal distress early!

question: Where are the parathyroid glands located?

options.A: Inside the left and right ventricles of the heart
options.B: On the posterior surface of the thyroid gland
options.C: At the upper poles of both adrenal glands
options.D: Suspended within the lower lobes of the lungs

explanation: You'll find these four tiny glands resting right on the back (posterior) side of your thyroid gland in the neck. You've got this!

question: Why are nurses often considered the central hub of the healthcare team?

options.A: They spend the most continuous time at the patient bedside
options.B: They make all the final diagnoses for hospital admissions
options.C: They hold the legal authority to hire and fire doctors
options.D: They control the entire hospital financial budget

explanation: That's right! Because nurses are right there by the bedside around the clock, we are usually the first to notice changes and connect all the other team members.

question: What is the main job of dietary fats in infants and toddlers?

options.A: Acting as the main fuel source for red blood cells
options.B: Preventing childhood obesity and sluggishness
options.C: Supporting central nervous system development and brain growth
options.D: Supplying all the necessary vitamin C for the immune system

explanation: Exactly! Little ones need healthy fats because their growing brains and nerves depend heavily on them for proper development.

question: At what point in your clinical workflow should healthcare waste be sorted?

options.A: At the final incineration site
options.B: During the weekly municipal garbage collection
options.C: After transport to the central landfill
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right where you use it! Doing it immediately stops dangerous items from getting mixed up with regular trash.

question: What should you do if asked to perform a task outside your training and scope of practice?

options.A: Decline the task based on your scope of practice
options.B: Perform it anyway to help out the busy department
options.C: Pretend you completed the task on the patient's chart
options.D: Ask a patient to teach you how to do it

explanation: Spot on! Always stay within your legal and certified scope of practice. Patient safety comes first, and it's okay to say no to things you aren't trained for yet.

question: Who makes up the control group in a case-control study?

options.A: People who refuse to participate
options.B: People with the disease
options.C: People without the disease
options.D: People currently receiving treatment

explanation: You nailed it! The control group acts as our healthy comparison baseline so we can see what was different about the people who got sick.

question: Which nursing action is best for stopping parasites from spreading through a community?

options.A: Ordering immediate major surgery for all children
options.B: Restricting patients from drinking clean tap water
options.C: Teaching proper handwashing and personal hygiene
options.D: Isolating infected patients in private hospital rooms

explanation: Good community education on handwashing and safe food habits cuts right through the fecal-oral chain of transmission. Excellent!

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of compact bone when compared to spongy bone?

options.A: It forms the dense and solid outer layer of bones
options.B: It contains an organized system of osteons
options.C: It has a high concentration of red bone marrow inside it
options.D: It provides major structural support for body weight

explanation: Red bone marrow is primarily housed within the open spaces of spongy bone, not inside dense compact bone. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h6)

question: What happens during a standard knee-jerk reflex test?

options.A: The sensory nerve is blocked, stopping all movement in the lower leg
options.B: The hamstring muscle is relaxed, causing the knee to bend backward
options.C: The quadriceps muscle is stretched, causing it to contract and kick the leg
options.D: The patellar tendon is compressed, causing the leg to go completely limp

explanation: When the patellar tendon gets a light tap, it stretches the quadriceps muscle. This quick stretch fires off a reflex that makes the leg kick forward naturally.

question: Why do ICUs often pause a patient's sedative medications for a short time every day?

options.A: To test the electrical activity of the heart muscles under stress
options.B: To allow family members to visit without medical equipment in the way
options.C: To ensure the patient has completely recovered from their primary disease
options.D: To reduce the duration of mechanical ventilation and prevent delirium

explanation: Giving a daily break from sedatives helps patients wake up sooner, get off the breathing machine faster, and stay mentally clear.

question: Why would a doctor order a stool culture for a patient with ongoing diarrhoea?

options.A: To isolate and identify specific bacterial or parasitic pathogens
options.B: To determine the patient's exact blood glucose level
options.C: To check for hidden microscopic blood in the stool
options.D: To measure the exact amount of daily fluid loss

explanation: A stool culture lets the lab grow whatever germs are hiding in the sample so the team knows exactly which bacteria or parasite is causing the trouble.

question: What is the primary goal of rehabilitation nursing?

options.A: To help patients regain their highest level of independence
options.B: To cure acute infectious diseases quickly
options.C: To provide permanent institutional care for the elderly
options.D: To manage chronic pain through heavy medication

explanation: Rehabilitation nursing focuses heavily on restoring a patient's functional abilities so they can care for themselves as much as possible. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h1)

question: What mask must you wear when entering a room under droplet precautions?

options.A: Double sterile surgical gloves
options.B: A full body hazardous materials suit
options.C: A fitted N95 respirator mask
options.D: A standard surgical or medical mask

explanation: Correct! A simple surgical mask does a great job blocking those heavy respiratory droplets from landing in your nose and mouth.

question: What emotional reaction do patients very commonly experience right after losing a limb?

options.A: Indifference to physical changes
options.B: Grief and a sense of loss
options.C: Complete memory loss
options.D: Immediate joyful acceptance

explanation: Losing a body part is a huge life change. Patients go through a normal grieving process, and it's our job to support them with empathy.

question: A patient calls saying she has soaked through two large sanitary pads every hour for three hours straight. What's your advice as the nurse?

options.A: Wait another six hours because heavy bleeding is always normal
options.B: Take another dose of misoprostol to finish the process
options.C: Apply a hot water bottle to the abdomen and rest in bed
options.D: Seek immediate medical evaluation for excessive bleeding

explanation: Soaking two heavy pads an hour for two hours in a row is our red flag for hemorrhage. Time to get them seen right away!

question: When giving ear drops to an adult patient, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna)?

options.A: Forward and down
options.B: Down and back
options.C: Straight outward
options.D: Up and back

explanation: A classic clinical tip! For adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the wiggly ear canal so the drops flow smoothly all the way down.

question: Which skin structure produces watery fluid to help cool the body through evaporation?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat cells
options.B: Eccrine sweat glands
options.C: Sebaceous glands
options.D: Arrector pili muscles

explanation: Great job! Eccrine sweat glands release water onto our skin, which cools us down as it evaporates into the air.

question: What underlying condition is the most frequent cause of oesophageal varices (enlarged veins)?

options.A: Portal hypertension from liver cirrhosis
options.B: Chronic bacterial infection of the stomach
options.C: Enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck
options.D: Severe long-term dietary iron deficiency

explanation: When the liver is scarred (cirrhosis), blood can't flow through it easily. This backs up pressure into nearby vessels, including the fragile veins in the oesophagus.

question: A stroke patient is trying to stick out their tongue, but it keeps pulling to one side. Which muscle is likely affected?

options.A: Palatoglossus
options.B: Hyoglossus
options.C: Genioglossus
options.D: Styloglossus

explanation: The genioglossus is our main tongue-poking muscle! When one side gets weak after a stroke, the tongue deviates toward the weaker side.

question: Where are our actual smell (olfactory) receptor cells located?

options.A: Inside the hard palate of the mouth
options.B: On the roof of the nasal cavity
options.C: Along the lower respiratory tract
options.D: Within the external ear canal

explanation: Spot on! The delicate olfactory epithelium holding our smell receptors sits high up near the roof of the nasal cavity, right where incoming air sweeps past.

question: Which of these is a great example of a well-written community health goal?

options.A: To teach nurses how to write better charts during night shifts
options.B: To reduce childhood malnutrition in Ward 4 by 20% within six months
options.C: To talk about malaria prevention whenever people visit the clinic
options.D: To make sure everybody in the whole country feels much healthier this year

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, tells you where it's happening, gives a clear percentage, and sets a realistic timeframe.

question: What happens when a vaccine gets too warm because the cold chain broke?

options.A: It expires in exactly one hour
options.B: It loses its potency permanently
options.C: It turns a bright neon color
options.D: It becomes safe to ingest orally

explanation: Heat damage can't be undone! Once a vaccine gets too warm, it won't protect the patient anymore, which is why keeping things cold is top priority.

question: A patient comes in with a swollen ulnar nerve and a numb patch on the arm. What should you suspect?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: A normal heat rash
options.C: Low blood levels (anemia)
options.D: Leprosy

explanation: When a nerve is thickened and a skin patch loses its feeling, leprosy should immediately come to mind. Spotting these clues makes you a great nurse!

question: What is an early sign of HIV-related changes in thinking and memory?

options.A: Sudden total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.B: Mild mental slowing and poor concentration
options.C: Auditory hallucinations and fixed delusions
options.D: Complete and permanent loss of speech

explanation: Early on, patients might just notice it's harder to focus, remember things, or think as quickly as usual.

question: Why must a nurse pull back the clothes and actually look at the patient's bare chest during a breathing assessment?

options.A: To listen for tummy sounds in the chest
options.B: To check the exact skin temperature
options.C: To check for chest symmetry, injuries, and odd movements
options.D: To get the skin ready for ECG stickers

explanation: Exactly! Looking closely helps you spot uneven chest rise, hidden wounds, or flail segments that make breathing difficult.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when collecting data?

options.A: Training all data collectors thoroughly before starting
options.B: Securing formal institutional approvals from management
options.C: Pilot testing questionnaires on a small sample group
options.D: Discarding digital backups immediately to save storage space

explanation: You nailed it! Deleting your backups is a huge risk that can lead to permanent data loss—definitely something we want to avoid!

question: When we talk about improving quality of life in home care, what should be our main focus?

options.A: Upgrading the client's home furniture and appliances
options.B: Eliminating all chronic health conditions completely
options.C: Strict adherence to hospital visiting hours
options.D: The client's personal values, dignity, and comfort

explanation: Exactly! Quality of life is all about keeping our clients comfortable, respected, and happy in their own space.

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pregnant women are legally required to visit the clinic every single week
options.B: It is impossible to eat a balanced diet without clinic supervision
options.C: Clinics require attendance records to secure international funding
options.D: Dangerous conditions like high blood pressure can develop without early warning signs

explanation: Exactly! Silent issues like pre-eclampsia or anemia can build up inside without any obvious signs at first. Routine checks keep both mum and baby safe.

question: Why are nurses in such a great position to catch adverse drug reactions early?

options.A: They are legally responsible for manufacturing all hospital drugs
options.B: They maintain close, continuous contact with hospitalized patients
options.C: They perform all laboratory blood chemistry tests
options.D: They set the retail prices for pharmaceuticals in Nigeria

explanation: Because you spend the most time right at the bedside, you are usually the first to notice early physical or mood changes after a patient takes a drug.

question: When is the best time for a patient on a high calorie diet to drink high-protein nutritional shakes?

options.A: Between meals so they do not crowd out solid food
options.B: Right in the middle of a heavy lunch or dinner
options.C: Immediately before going to sleep at night
options.D: Only when the patient feels intensely thirsty

explanation: Drinking supplements between meals prevents the stomach from filling up with liquids before the patient can eat solid food. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h6)

question: What role do normal bacterial flora play in the healthy vagina?

options.A: They assist with the physical transport of sperm cells
options.B: They supply blood directly to the uterine lining
options.C: They maintain an acidic environment to protect against pathogens
options.D: They produce hormones to regulate the menstrual cycle

explanation: Good bacteria like Lactobacillus produce acid, which stops harmful bacteria and fungi from multiplying. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h2)
